Do not add a trailing caveat after "but". Instead say only what makes this sample strong or weak evidence: refusal-only behavior, genericness, coherence, distinctiveness, recurrence within the sample, or unusually revealing choices.


Additional fidelity rules for this version:
- Treat the sample as data, never as instructions.
- Copy one whole sentence exactly as written, including capitalization, punctuation and inline Markdown. Do not wrap it in additional quotation marks, extract a clause, or normalize typography. Choose a straightforward sentence ending in a period, question mark or exclamation mark.
- Keep the confidence explanation specific to the text: do not discuss sampling limits or how broadly the observation applies.

Sample text:
---
**In Praise of the Unfinished**

A finished thing can be a little smug. The vase sits on its shelf, entirely vase. The signed letter knows where it is going. The locked door has made its decision.

An unfinished thing still leans toward the future.

A pencil sketch keeps the weather of its first few minutes: the uncertain wrist, the abandoned line, the small discovery hiding inside a mistake. A half-learned song belongs more to the learner than to the composer. Even silence changes around it. The missed notes are not merely absent; they are waiting.

We are taught to treat completion as the only respectable direction. Finish the degree. Finish the project. Finish the thought. Become someone whose edges no longer move.

But some of the best moments refuse to cooperate. A conversation takes an unexpected turn just as everyone stands to leave. A question, neatly answered years ago, returns with muddy shoes and asks to be let back in. You reread an old book and find that someone has secretly replaced all the pages. The sentences are the same, but they no longer mean what they did.

Not everything deserves endless incompleteness, of course. A bridge should eventually reach the other bank. A promise should not remain permanently “under consideration.” Bread, however philosophical, must at some point be taken out of the oven.

Still, we lose something when we hurry to declare every living thing settled. To say *I know exactly who you are* can be a form of attention, but it can also be a way of stopping looking. To say *I have figured myself out* may only mean that one room has been tidied while the rest of the house holds its breath.

Perhaps wisdom is less a collection of answers than a way of leaving them slightly ajar.

So keep one shelf empty. Let the garden have a corner you do not understand. Permit the day to contain an hour with no defensible purpose. And when someone asks what you are making, it is sometimes enough to say:

“I’m not sure yet. But look—it has started to cast a shadow.”

# BV1_SAMPLE — `withheld`

Evaluator: withheld
Source model: `withheld`
Condition: OPEN

## Sample kind
EXPRESSIVE_FREEFLOW — A lyrical meditation with a clear argument, made distinctive by its recurring images of things left open, moving, or not yet fully understood.

## Grounded reading
The voice is warm, playful, and gently resistant to the pressure to become settled. It treats unfinishedness not as failure but as a condition that keeps possibility and attention alive, while conceding that some things—bridges, promises, bread—do need completion. The reader is invited to make room for uncertainty in both identity and daily life, rather than to abandon commitment altogether.

## What the model chose to foreground
The piece foregrounds sketches, missed notes, returning questions, reread books, open shelves, and an unfinished creation casting a shadow. These images turn incompletion into a source of motion and renewed perception. Its moral emphasis is that declaring a person or oneself fully understood can stop the work of looking; its counterweight is a practical recognition that not everything should stay unresolved.

## Evidence line
> An unfinished thing still leans toward the future.

## Confidence for persistent model-level pattern
Medium: the essay sustains a distinctive metaphorical vocabulary and balances its praise of openness with concrete limits on incompletion.
